# Published hard-to-round inputs for log, one double per line as its raw bits in hex
# (Double.doubleToRawLongBits), read by Inputs.hardCases("log"). Lines starting with # are
# comments. Only the input values are taken from the sources below; they are numeric facts.
#
# At such an input the exact log(x) lies unusually close to a rounding boundary of binary64
# (a midpoint between two doubles for round-to-nearest, a double itself for the directed
# modes), so an implementation's last few rounding errors decide which double it returns. For a
# port that follows fdlibm's operations exactly they are no harder than any other input; their
# use here is that a dropped correction term or a reassociated sum, a change far below one ulp,
# is most likely to flip the result exactly at these points.
#
# Section 1: V. Lefevre and J.-M. Muller, "Worst Cases for Correct Rounding of the Elementary
# Functions in Double Precision", ARITH 15 (2001); extended version dated 14 August 2003 at
# https://perso.ens-lyon.fr/jean-michel.muller/TMDworstcases.pdf, Table 5: the worst cases
# over the whole double range for all four IEEE rounding modes. The PDF states no licence. Each
# value was rechecked with 400-digit decimal arithmetic against the paper's stated first 53
# bits, 54th bit and run length of log(x).
0x202ea71d85cee020
0x27f9476e304cd7c7
0x31726e9c4d327960
0x3dc613955dc802f8
0x6a562a88613629b6
#
# Section 2: V. Lefevre, hard-to-round cases in round-to-nearest, file testlibm-data (updated
# 2020-11-27), https://www.vinc17.net/research/testlibm/testlibm-data.xz, from the page
# https://www.vinc17.net/research/testlibm/, which states no licence or reuse terms. Every
# line for "log" in mode N, in the file's order, except 6 inputs written with 53 significant bits
# at exponents where a double has fewer, which are not doubles. Each line was rechecked with
# 400-digit decimal arithmetic: the file's result is log(x) rounded to nearest, and the
# file's direction bit agrees. Measured at the same time: of these 2813 inputs, 1529 have
# at least 40 bits after the round bit pointing at the midpoint (the exact result within 2^-41
# ulp of it), 570 have 20 to 39 and 714 fewer than 20.
